deviations.baseline_behavior: ConsoleHost parses switches that widen access (for example -noprofile, -executionpolicy, -configurationfile, server modes) from the command line, then starts; policy applies after parsing.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Load policy from a signed source first; refuse switches that widen access when lockdown is on; refuse server modes without an authenticated transport.
deviations.benefit: Closes a path where a launch argument weakens a locked-down start.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Scripts that pass widening switches under lockdown stop working.

deviations.baseline_behavior: ConsoleHost carries Windows-only pieces: ConsoleControl Win32 calls, jump list, -windowstyle, -sta by default, Hyper-V socket modes.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Leave them out of the first version.
deviations.compatibility_cost: No Windows console extras, no Hyper-V mode.

deviations.baseline_behavior: The default embedded session is full language with all commands visible.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Default embedded session is restricted; full language needs an explicit opt-in.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Embedders must opt in to the full session.

deviations.baseline_behavior: PSRP carries XML payloads, fragments, in-protocol key exchange and priority streams over several transports.
deviations.proposed_behavior: No remoting in the first version; if added later, use a typed binary protocol with transport-level authentication.
deviations.benefit: Removes a large attack surface and a large unverified area.

deviations.baseline_behavior: Transports: WSMan (native plugin), SSH subsystem, named pipe, Hyper-V socket, container and VM process.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Omit WSMan, Hyper-V and container transports; consider SSH-style process stdio first if remoting is added.

deviations.baseline_behavior: CLIXML reader has depth limits but no explicit maximum input size; depth-1 property bags can include sensitive properties.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Add a maximum input size and streaming limit to the reader; mark sensitive properties so shallow bags cannot leak them.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Large documents fail to import unless a limit is raised.

deviations.baseline_behavior: Role merging concatenates values from all matching roles; there is no deny rule.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Add explicit deny rules with deny-over-allow precedence and a report of effective capabilities.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Role files need a deny section; merge results change when deny is used.

deviations.baseline_behavior: OS differences are spread over 390 conditional blocks and many runtime queries.
deviations.proposed_behavior: One platform interface with a runtime capability table; conditional compilation only inside interface implementations.
deviations.benefit: Testable on every OS; one place to review.

deviations.baseline_behavior: Native layer: hand-kept struct layouts for libpsl-native, three interop styles, C source in another repository.
deviations.proposed_behavior: One native surface per OS with generated bindings and a layout test in CI.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Build tooling must generate and verify bindings.

deviations.baseline_behavior: Last-resort resolver loads <rid>/<name>.<ext> from the folder of the calling assembly with no signature or location check.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Prefer the application directory and a signed or pinned per-RID folder; refuse writable locations unless policy allows.
deviations.benefit: Blocks library planting through writable module folders.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Modules with native libraries need a signed or allowed location.

deviations.baseline_behavior: Zone checks and the execution-policy store exist only on Windows; Unix treats every file as local and cannot set a policy.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Define origin and policy for every supported OS, or report 'not enforced' through one status API.
deviations.benefit: Security behavior is the same or explicitly different per OS.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Unix users get a policy store and origin marks.
